summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, the 13th Dalai Lama studied under teachers including Agvan Dorzhiev, Tertön Sogyal, Pa Ri Rabsal, and Yeshe Chopel, and taught numerous students, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 1st Beru Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He taught numerous students, including 2nd Beru Khyentse and Reginald A. Ray.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche studied under Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, Khangsar Dorje Chang, and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, 2nd Beru Khyentse studied under teachers including Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche (~1960–1989), the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse.
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

Specializing in Indology, A. A. Krishnaswami Ayyangar studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1907–1911). He taught at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore from 1918 to 1947.

Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, A. Aiyappan studied at the University of Madras (~1925–1927). He served as superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1966–1969).
Specializing in Indology and philosophy, A. Anantacharya served as a pandit at the Mysore Archaeological Department and was attested as head of Yatiraja Mutt in 1926.
An Indologist, A. B. Gajendragadkar held posts as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

Muller specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. After earning his Ph.D. at Stony Brook University, he held posts at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).
Working in Indology and religious studies, A. G. Mohan studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1971 to 1989. In 1976, he founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram.

A philosopher who earned his B.A. from Jesus College, Cambridge, Armstrong held positions including Professor of Classics at the University of Malta (1939) and Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).

Narain worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD from SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1971 to 1987.

A scholar in linguistics and Indology, A. K. Ramanujan studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Indiana University (PhD). He held multiple faculty posts at the University of Chicago between 1962 and 1983.
Specializing in Tibetology, A. M. D'Rozario earned an M.Sc. from the University of Allahabad and a Ph.D. from the University of Cambridge.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, A. Mahadeva Sastri served as curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and director at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

An Indologist who studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar, A. N. Krishna Aiyangar served as joint editor for Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

Specializing in linguistics and Indology, A. N. Narasimhia completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner. He later served as librarian and part-time professor of philology at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and held a post at the University of Mysore.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, A. P. Buddhadatta was a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya (attested 1923) and worked as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College.

An Indologist and archaeologist, A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar worked as an epigraphical assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941) and served as superintendent of the Department of Archaeology, Travancore State, in 1922.
